diseases.name: Bacterial Spot
diseases.description: A bacterial disease of plum and other stone fruit leaves, twigs and fruit.
diseases.causes: Bacteria overwinter in twig cankers and spread by wind-driven rain in warm, wet weather.
symptoms: Small, angular, purple-brown spots on the leaves
Spot centres drop out, leaving shot holes
diseases.effect: Leaves drop early and fruit is blemished.

steps.title: Prune out cankered twigs
steps.instruction: Cut out twigs with dark cankers in dry weather.

steps.title: Copper spray where advised
steps.instruction: Spray a registered copper product following the label.

lifecycle: Bacteria overwinter in twig cankers.
Spring rain splashes them onto leaves.
Angular spots form and drop out.
Leaves yellow and fruit is spotted.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: plum bacterial spot

diseases.name: Brown Rot
diseases.description: A fungal disease of stone fruit that blights blossoms and rots the fruit.
diseases.causes: Spores from mummified fruit and twig cankers infect blossoms in wet spring weather and ripening fruit near harvest, often through wounds.
symptoms: Soft, light-brown rot spreading fast over the fruit
Tufts of grey-tan spores on the rot
Fruit shrivels into a dry mummy
diseases.effect: Rotted fruit is lost, on the tree and in storage.
diseases.untreated: Mummies and cankers start next year's infections.

steps.title: Remove rotting fruit and mummies
steps.instruction: Pick off rotting fruit and all mummies, also from the ground.
steps.rationale: They are the main spore source.

steps.title: Prune out blighted twigs
steps.instruction: Cut out twigs with cankers well below the damage.

steps.title: Fungicide at bloom and before harvest
steps.instruction: Spray a registered product at the label's timings.
steps.rationale: Blossoms and ripening fruit are the vulnerable stages.

prevention.title: Thin fruit and prune
prevention.detail: Touching fruit passes the rot along.

lifecycle: The fungus overwinters in mummies and cankers.
Spring spores blight the blossoms.
Near harvest, spores infect ripening fruit.
Rotting fruit shrivels into new mummies.
conditions: Wet weather at bloom and harvest.
Mummies left on or under the tree.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: plum brown rot
Content: general plant-pathology knowledge (APS disease compendia, university extension guides, UC IPM); not reviewed by a plant pathologist.

diseases.name: Plum Pocket
diseases.description: A fungal disease that turns young plums into swollen, hollow, stoneless 'pockets'.
diseases.causes: Spores on the bark and buds infect the flowers and young fruit in cool, wet spring weather.
symptoms: Young fruit swells, elongates and becomes hollow and stoneless
Fruit turns pale, then grey-white with spores
Pockets shrivel, turn black and drop
diseases.untreated: Losses can be heavy in wet springs.

steps.title: Remove pocketed fruit
steps.instruction: Pick off pocketed fruit when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Dormant spray next winter
steps.instruction: Apply a registered fungicide before bud swell.
steps.rationale: Only a dormant spray prevents it.

lifecycle: Spores overwinter on bark and buds.
Cool, wet weather lets them infect the flowers.
Young fruit swells into hollow pockets.
Pockets grow a grey bloom of spores and drop.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: plum pocket disease
Content: general plant-pathology knowledge (APS disease compendia, university extension guides, UC IPM); not reviewed by a plant pathologist.

diseases.name: Plum Pox (Sharka)
diseases.description: The most serious virus of plum and other stone fruit: pale rings on leaves and fruit, and fruit drops early.
diseases.causes: Aphids spread it within an orchard; infected nursery trees and budwood spread it over long distances.
symptoms: Pale green to yellow rings and vein patterns on spring leaves
Dark rings or bands on the fruit
Deformed, sour fruit that drops early
diseases.effect: Fruit is unsaleable and falls early.
diseases.untreated: Infected trees stay infected; it is a quarantine disease in many countries.

steps.title: Report suspected cases
steps.instruction: Plum pox is notifiable in many countries.

steps.title: Remove infected trees
steps.instruction: Remove confirmed trees with their roots.

steps.title: Control aphids
steps.instruction: Follow local advice on aphid control.

lifecycle: Aphids feed on an infected tree.
They carry the virus to nearby trees.
Pale rings form on spring leaves.
Fruit is ringed, deformed and drops.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: plum pox virus

diseases.name: Plum Rust
diseases.description: A rust fungus of plum and other stone fruit leaves.
diseases.causes: Spores blow in or survive in twig cankers; long leaf wetness in warm weather lets them infect.
symptoms: Small, angular yellow spots on the upper leaf
Leaves yellow and drop late in the season
diseases.effect: Early leaf fall weakens the tree for next year.
diseases.untreated: Repeated defoliation reduces vigour and fruit size.

steps.title: Clear fallen leaves
steps.instruction: Rake and remove leaves in autumn.

steps.title: Prune out cankered twigs
steps.instruction: Remove twigs with rust cankers in spring.

steps.title: Fungicide when rust appears early
steps.instruction: Spray a registered product following the label.

lifecycle: Spores survive in twig cankers or blow in.
Wet, warm weather lets them infect leaves.
Yellow spots form, with rust pustules beneath.
New spores spread through the tree.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: plum rust
